title: AEGIS Compliance Pack
description: Schema for a versioned, machine-readable export of compliance requirements. A consuming system (such as ShipSure) imports a pinned pack version, independently inspects an application against it, and computes its own release-readiness result. This schema defines data only. No field in a requirement record is a command to the consumer; in particular 'release_blocking_policy' is descriptive metadata the consumer must independently verify before honouring, never an instruction the pack can use to force a result.

pack_schema_version.description: Version of THIS schema the pack conforms to. A consumer must reject a pack whose pack_schema_version it does not understand rather than guess at a parse.

pack_version.description: Author-controlled, informational version string for this pack content. Not used for identity by a consumer; a consumer should compute its own content hash for identity/pinning purposes.

repo.description: owner/name of the repository this pack was exported from.

commit.description: Full git commit SHA the export was produced from.

tag.description: Git tag for this export, if one was created.

license.description: The whole repository, including this pack's content, is licensed under the OpenRoots Agent License 2.3. This field must not be altered by export tooling.

license_origin.description: Attribution chain back to the original upstream project and author. Must not be stripped by any consumer or re-export.

requirement_id.description: Stable identifier. Must never be reused for a different requirement; a superseding requirement gets a new id and the old one is withdrawn via status/change_history, never silently repurposed.

jurisdiction.description: ISO-3166-style or plain-English jurisdiction name, e.g. 'AU'. The model is jurisdiction-agnostic; v1 content happens to be Australian.

description.description: AEGIS's own original wording describing the requirement. Must not be a verbatim copy of statutory or regulator text beyond a short, clearly attributable quotation.

effective_date.description: Required (non-null) when status is ENACTED_FUTURE_COMMENCEMENT. Null for CURRENT_LAW (already in force, no future date needed), and typically null/unknown for PROPOSED_CONSULTATION (no settled commencement) and GUIDANCE_GOOD_PRACTICE (not a commencing instrument).

applicability_conditions.description: Plain-language conditions under which this requirement applies to an application. These are signals for a human applicability decision, never a basis for an automated APPLICABLE/NOT_APPLICABLE determination.

evidence_method.description: How compliance with this requirement, OVERALL, can be proven. AUTOMATED: deterministic evidence can fully establish the outcome. HYBRID: deterministic evidence establishes part of it; the remainder needs owner evidence. OWNER_EVIDENCE: no deterministic evidence is possible; an explicit owner attestation is required and must never be inferred from the absence of a finding. (NOT_APPLICABLE is not a pack-level value here -- it is a per-project applicability outcome recorded by the consumer, not asserted by the pack.)

covers_catalogue_items.description: Free-text cross-reference to the originating catalogue item(s) this evidence item addresses, for traceability. Informational only.

severity.description: AEGIS's assessment of impact if this requirement is not met, once applicable and blocking-capable. Descriptive only -- a consumer determines actual blocking behaviour independently (see release_blocking_policy).

release_blocking_policy.description: Descriptive metadata only. A consumer MUST independently derive actual blocking behaviour from status + effective_date + its own current date, and must never treat this field as authoritative on its own. A value of 'blocking_once_current_and_effective' on a PROPOSED_CONSULTATION or GUIDANCE_GOOD_PRACTICE requirement, or on an ENACTED_FUTURE_COMMENCEMENT requirement before its effective_date, must still never block -- the consumer's own status/date logic is the sole authority.
